Schema builds

Find the firmware builds your appliances run that SATOM has never harvested, harvest them in one click, and see what changed against the closest known build.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsregistry.view appliances.apply
📍 Whereany ADOM → Automation → API → Schema builds; API → Schema builds for profiles without write access (Global ADOM: inside the Global block) (URL /schema-builds/); bell notification "New build … schema not harvested"

What is it?#

Every Fortinet product describes its configuration schema differently. SATOM has one schema adapter per product that turns it into the same per-build, per-channel model of the API library. Schema builds shows the adapters, the builds your appliances run that have no harvested schema yet, and — after a harvest — what changed against the closest build SATOM already knew.

What does it do?#

  • When an appliance reports a build with no harvested schema, every administrator gets one bell notification for that product and build: New build 8.0.7 on fweb-01: schema not harvested. It is not repeated for the next appliance on the same build.
  • Lists each adapter with its Capabilities and its Verification — on which device and build it was checked against real hardware:
Product CLI schema REST schema Verification
FortiWeb tree probe of every tree object verified (7.6.8, 8.0.6)
FortiAuthenticator set ? help walk of the setup CLI API schema verified (8.0.3)
FortiGate tree ?action=schema verified (8.0.1); evidence by pack or import, not live
FortiADC tree (FortiWeb format) read-only shape probe of the tree objects the rediscovery sweep lacks: top-level objects, and child tables by ?pkey= verified (7.6.7 build0676, {device}, 2026-10-13: 527 objects; path rule held for 224 of 225 REST endpoints)
FortiAnalyzer JSON-RPC syntax same verified (7.6.7 build3737, {device}: 139 objects read)
  • Offers a Harvest button per appliance on an unharvested build.
  • After a harvest, compares the new build with the closest harvested build of the same product: every new or changed object and field, and its Channel on the new build.

Requirements#

  • The appliance's firmware has been read (the firmware probe records the build).
  • For a harvest: the appliance is reachable over SSH (and REST for the REST probe) with the credentials SATOM holds. FortiAuthenticator also needs its CLI password for the CLI half (see below).

Permissions#

Action Needs
Open the page registry.view
Harvest appliances.apply
Receive the bell notification administrators (user management)

The sidebar entry is shown in every ADOM to holders of registry.view: under Automation → API when you have write access, otherwise in the API group (an API sub-menu inside the Global block in the Global ADOM).

How to use#

Harvest a new build#

  1. Open the notification, or Automation → API → Schema builds in the sidebar (without write access: API → Schema builds).
  2. Under Builds without a harvested schema, find the appliance.
  3. For a FortiAuthenticator, fill CLI password (optional) if you want its CLI schema too.
  4. Click Harvest. The harvest is read-only on the box.
  5. Read the comparison: the new build compared with the closest harvested build, item by item.

Read the comparison#

Column Means
Object / Field what was added, removed or changed
Change added, removed, options, type, range, default, rename candidate
Channel on the new build both, CLI only, hidden, REST only — or unknown — to verify when REST was not measured on the new build yet

Use Compare with to pick another harvested build.

Example#

🧪Example — An appliance is upgraded to a build nobody harvested

After a firmware upgrade, fweb-07 runs 8.0.7. The bell shows New build 8.0.7 on fweb-07: schema not harvested. An administrator opens Schema builds, clicks Harvest on fweb-07, and reads the comparison with 8.0.6: four new fields in the bot-detection policy, one enum option removed. Build compatibility and the migration report now answer for 8.0.7.

Result#

  • New cli_tree / cli_full (and REST probe) evidence for that build in the API library; the build appears under Harvested builds.
  • An audit entry schema_builds.harvest.
  • The appliance leaves the pending list.

Troubleshooting#

"Every appliance runs a build whose schema is harvested."#

Nothing to do: no pending build.

The harvest of a FortiAuthenticator read REST but not the CLI#

Possible causes - SATOM stores the FortiAuthenticator REST API key, which cannot log into the CLI.

Solution 1. Harvest again with CLI password (optional) filled in. It is used for that harvest only and never stored.

A FortiGate shows "pack / import" instead of a Harvest button#

Possible causes - FortiGate's CLI tree arrives only by knowledge pack or import: the FortiGate workspace only reads configuration. (Its REST ?action=schema IS read live, by the API-library harvest — see API library.)

Solution 1. Import a knowledge pack that covers the build, or import saved captures with flask apilib schema-import (see API library).

A FortiAnalyzer harvest says "stored as unhealthy"#

Possible causes - The syntax walk read nothing, was refused or broke. The record is kept, as an unhealthy evidence row, and the reason is named: firmware_unknown (the box did not report its build on /sys/status), no_catalog (SATOM knows no FortiAnalyzer object to ask about), walk_failed, no_objects, refused (the API user lacks read access) or no_client (no session).

Solution 1. no_catalog: import the FortiAnalyzer API library or a knowledge pack first. 2. refused / no_client: check the appliance's API user and credentials on its device page, then harvest again. 3. The build always comes from the box itself, never from the inventory row, so a wrong firmware string in the inventory does not change the result.

"unverified adapter"#

Possible causes - The product's adapter was never checked against a device. Every adapter in the table above is verified (FortiADC since 2026-10-13, on 7.6.7 build0676), so this badge appears only for an adapter added later without a lab check.

Solution 1. Treat its results as a documented convention, not a measurement.

A FortiADC child table is missing from the REST shape probe#

Possible causes - FortiADC serves some child tables only inside the parent row; their child path answers 404. The probe does not record a child 404 as absent, so the fields are not turned into false CLI only entries. Paths that the device treats as actions (FortiADC reboots and resets through some GETs), objects nested more than one table deep and children of an empty table are skipped as well.

Solution 1. Nothing to fix: those fields stay unknown until other evidence (the rediscovery sweep's row) measures them.

Many new items read "unknown — to verify"#

Possible causes - REST has not been measured on the new build for those objects (empty tables).

Solution 1. Expected. A sweep, a REST probe or a knowledge pack fills them in.

Advanced#

Advanced Watch and scheduled actions

services/schema_watch.py runs after every firmware read and from the schema_watch scheduled action; it never raises into its caller. The schema_harvest scheduled action harvests pending builds, FortiAuthenticator and FortiAnalyzer through their adapters. Neither action is scheduled by default — create a schedule under Scheduled actions. Shell: flask apilib adapter-harvest <appliance> [--ssh-secret-env VAR]; flask apilib schema-harvest and satom execute apilib harvest take the same adapter path for a FortiAnalyzer or FortiAuthenticator (they answered "unsupported" before 3.3.1).

Advanced Read-only by construction

The FortiAuthenticator walk can send only ? questions, config <object> and edit <a row the box listed>; never set <value>, next, end or abort, and it drops the session after each object. FortiWeb, FortiADC and FortiGate harvests send tree (behind its own gate) and show.

#schema builds#new firmware#new build#harvest#schema adapter#tree#cli schema#notification#schema_watch#schema_harvest#verified#unverified
